newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt market quiet, MCI tightens.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt market quiet, MCI tightens.

text.p: The market in U.S. corporate high-yield and investment-grade bonds experienced a quiet day on Friday after digesting $6 to $7 billion in new supply earlier in the week, dealers said.
MCI Corp and MobileMedia Corp debt saw particularly active trading, however.

Traders said senior debt of MCI tightened by around 7 basis points in afternoon trading as a result of speculation that a potential merger between the company and British Telecommunications would cause rating agencies to upgrade MCI debt.
Frank Plumley, director at Standard & Poor's hinted that the market's speculation may be on target.

"BT is rated triple-A and MCI is rated single-A. In the event of a merger we would expect the gap to close. As to where it will shake out, that will depend on the terms of the deal and the source of the funding." he said.
The affects of the merger news spilled over into the high-yield market, with prices among junk telecommunications and cable sector bonds rising by 3/4 to one point by the end of Friday.

MobileMedia bonds were off by only around one point at the end of Friday trading, after having plummeted by eight to nine points earlier in the day. The company announced Friday morning that it planned to miss an $11.7 million November 1 interest payment, a trader said.
Analysts said the bonds recovered most of their losses because of optimistic statements made by the company that it may make the payment before the end of a 30-day grace period.
Overall, prices in the junk market improved by approximately 1/4 of a point on news that inflows into high-yield mutual funds were continuing at a healthy pace.
In the primary market for junk issues, Brooks Fiber Properties Inc sold $225 million of 11 7/8 percent zero coupon bonds in a 144a private placement through Goldman Sachs.
Motors and Gears Inc sold $170 million in 10 3/4 percent senior subordinated notes in a 144a offering via Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
In the investment grade area, Champion International Corp sold $200 million in Baa1/BBB-rated 7.20 percent bonds through Goldman Sachs on Friday.
Goldman also lead a $800 million 144a offering of investment grade debt for Levi Stauss on Friday, sources say.
